clue.text: Massage includes back exercises, giving protection for joints

indicators.note: the massage word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to massage dough or muscles is to knead them

indicators.note: back tells us the exercises abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: PE, physical education, means exercises

explanation.surface: A physio works on a patient's back with massage and exercises, then hands over something to protect the joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PE into EP, which goes inside KNEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneepad is padding strapped over the knee, one of the body's main joints, to shield it.

clue.text: Type to apprehend sons with a slap, and be reconciled

indicators.note: apprehend means seize and hold, so the type word holds the next letters

parts.note: kind means type or sort
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for sons
slap is theatrical slang for make-up

explanation.surface: A father who takes his sons in hand with a slap, then makes peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slap' looks violent but is actors' slang for greasepaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and make up is an idiom for ending a quarrel and becoming friends again.

clue.text: Excited to get to entertain one's number one fan

indicators.note: to entertain is to receive in, so the anagram holds the next piece
excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one gives I, and 's gives S

explanation.surface: An excited supporter can't wait to meet the star they idolise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' rearranges TO GET as EGOTT, around IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-obsessed person is their own biggest admirer, so 'number one' means oneself.

clue.text: Perhaps someone you can't have begun to analyse mentally

indicators.note: begun points to the initial letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a person who is beyond any attempt at psychoanalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych someone is to work out or analyse their state of mind, from psychology slang.

clue.text: Low-key opening for dignitary to have to attend

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to own something is to have it
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: A quiet start for a dignitary who must attend an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' hints at a musical sense of the answer, but it just takes D from 'dignitary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat describes a subdued, unemphatic or gloomy mood, close to understated.

clue.text: Horror-struck scallywag has turned to bottle

indicators.note: to bottle is to keep something contained, so the answer sits inside the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled to find that a young rascal has taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like a reversal signal but is just part of the run: scallywAG HAS Turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone stricken with shock and dismay, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Area of land abroad that's cut too fine

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: also means too
ace means excellent, very fine

explanation.surface: A foreign plot of land has been sliced up too thinly.
explanation.walkthrough: ALSO cut short gives ALS; 'cut too fine' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region of north-eastern France on the German border, a foreign territory to a British solver.

clue.text: Be constrained to make shamefaced attempt to succeed?

parts.note: to have to do something is to be constrained to do it
to abash someone is to embarrass them

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to shame a person who is trying to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash is British slang for having a go or trying something out.

clue.text: Spades, etc, put out as diamonds often

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player lays out spades and so on, as is common with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges S, ETC and PUT. 'diamonds' suggests the card suit, but it means gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A step cut is a gem style with rows of parallel facets, often given to diamonds and emeralds.

clue.text: Pig squeals, circling an unspecified number of birds

indicators.note: the pig word goes round the number letter

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
yowls are loud wailing cries, like squeals

explanation.surface: A pig squeals while running rings round a flock of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowy owls are large white Arctic owls, so they are an example of birds.

clue.text: Even features of event, etc, OK as alternative to polo?

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and so on, of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fashion note on what to wear to an event: something else will do instead of polo.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of eVeNt, eTc and OK gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A V-shaped neckline is a choice of jumper collar one might pick instead of a polo neck.

clue.text: Criticise person very loudly: shocking treatment that brings censequences

definitions.note: the clue's plural noun for results that follow, matched by a singular phrase naming such results

parts.note: to knock something is to criticise it
one means a person
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: Someone loudly condemns electric shock treatment for its after-effects.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper printed 'censequences', a misprint for consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock-on effect is a secondary result that follows indirectly from an action, a chain of outcomes.

clue.text: Scotsman's first hour spent finding members of sect

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so this letter is taken away

parts.note: Hamish is a typically Scottish first name; the 's is 'is', a link

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word hour

explanation.surface: A Scotsman spends his first hour searching for members of a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamish is a stock Scottish name; removing H (the first letter of 'hour') leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a Mennonite Christian sect in America known for shunning modern technology.

clue.text: Author's life-story opened with old article in series of chapters

indicators.note: the life-story word is opened up to take the following letters

parts.note: a bio is a short biography

indicators.note: the article sits inside the chapters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter, so a run of them gives CCCC
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer's biography opens with an old piece in a run of chapters.
explanation.walkthrough: BIO is split after B to take O plus CC A CC; the 's after Author is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Boccaccio was the 14th-century Italian writer of the Decameron.

clue.text: European press to pay after boxing match fixed

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the pressing word goes round the rest

parts.note: to dun someone is to press them to pay a debt

indicators.note: a fixed match has been rigged, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports reporter is pressed to pay up after a rigged boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges MATCH as TCHMA, and 'boxing' puts it inside DUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutchman is a man from the Netherlands, so he is an example of a European.

clue.text: Sound of horn unknown with hit piano music

parts.note: a honk is the noise a car horn makes
Y is an algebraic unknown
tonk is slang for hit hard

explanation.surface: A car horn blares, drowning out the piano playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Honky-tonk is a ragtime style of piano playing, often on a tinny upright in a bar.

clue.text: Writer of musicals to pass for classical composer

parts.note: Lionel Bart wrote the musical Oliver!
to OK something is to approve or pass it

explanation.surface: A writer of stage musicals is mistaken for a serious classical composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian twentieth-century composer of orchestral and chamber works.

clue.text: Forgiving one for tale-telling

parts.note: reads as someone excusing a gossip, but points to a forgiver of sins who tells a story in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales

explanation.surface: Someone who lets off a snitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval seller of indulgences forgave sins, and Chaucer gives one such pilgrim a tale to tell.

clue.text: Excellent tongue that's been chopped poorly

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the last letter of the tongue word goes

parts.note: lingo means a language or tongue

explanation.surface: A fine piece of tongue has been badly chopped up in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' looks like an adverb on the chopping, but it is the definition in its British sense of unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use 'poorly' means unwell, so it matches being sick or in failing health.

clue.text: Italian learning drama taking in character at the end

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the drama word holds the letter

parts.note: No, or Noh, is classical Japanese drama
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An Italian student of drama takes on a role in the final scene.
explanation.walkthrough: NO (Japanese Noh drama) takes in Z, the alphabet's last character.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorenzo is a common Italian man's name, as in Lorenzo de' Medici, so it is an example of an Italian.

clue.text: Courses for auditors almost all lack attraction for the rich?

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is as heard

parts.note: tacks are the courses a sailing boat steers

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: '(we) haven't' says that everyone lacks something

explanation.surface: Accountancy courses are almost useless at drawing in wealthy clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' suggests accountants, but here means listeners. HAVEN'T loses its last letter to give HAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-tax country lures wealthy people and companies to park their money there.

clue.text: Instrument of long ago, a case of terrible disregard

parts.note: the viol is a bowed string instrument of the Renaissance

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: An antique instrument shows a terrible lack of care.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a rule or law is to break it, ignoring it entirely.

clue.text: A trick juggling wheels one buys in parts

indicators.note: juggling means tossing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus act in which someone juggles wheels bought one part at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A kit car is a vehicle sold as a set of components for the owner to assemble.

clue.text: Library arranged for journalist to ring one up in good time

indicators.note: ring means encircle, so the journalist goes round the rest

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A library is reorganised so a journalist can phone someone in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles LIBRARY into ARLYBIR, which ED surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An early riser is someone who is up and about ahead of others, as in the proverb about catching the worm.

clue.text: Greedily consume small drink, but no drugs

indicators.note: no says these letters are taken out

parts.note: coffee is a drink
E is slang for ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down a small drink, but stays off the drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: COFFEE without its two Es (ecstasy tablets) gives COFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat something quickly and greedily, wolfing it down.

clue.text: Head of Scotland Yard team

indicators.note: head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a quad, or quadrangle, is a courtyard

explanation.surface: The chief of Scotland Yard's team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotland Yard' reads as the London police, but the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a small group working together, especially in sport or the police.

clue.text: Put out by biting attack from the right? One might be

definitions.text: Put out by biting attack from the right? One might be

indicators.note: read from the right, the biting word goes backwards

parts.note: a nip is a small bite
KO, knockout, means put out

explanation.surface: Someone stung by a right-wing attack: the kind of person who would be.
explanation.walkthrough: NIP read from the right gives PIN; KO follows. The whole clue describes a mild leftie, the natural target of attacks from the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinko is a derogatory term for someone with left-leaning politics, a typical target for the right.

clue.text: Maybe go through mood changes of criminal: prison worried

definitions.text: Maybe go through mood changes of

parts.note: a con is a convict
jug is slang for prison
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: A convict's moods swing wildly; the prison is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mood' here is grammatical: a verb's indicative, subjunctive and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjugate a verb is to list its forms through tenses, persons and grammatical moods.

clue.text: Chestnut that can come from the best or worst of commentators

indicators.note: commentators speak, so the word is as it sounds

parts.note: to best or to worst someone both mean to defeat them

explanation.surface: An old joke that might come from either the finest or the poorest sports commentators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnut' suggests a tired old joke; 'worst' here is the verb meaning defeat. A conker is the horse chestnut seed British children play a game with on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The shiny brown seed of the horse chestnut tree is called a conker in Britain.

clue.text: Redecorated skips one time in New York, say: most colourful

indicators.note: skips means leaves out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to redo a room is to redecorate it
I is the Roman numeral for one
EST is Eastern Standard Time, used in New York

explanation.surface: A New York apartment, redecorated for a while, ends up the most colourful of all.
explanation.walkthrough: REDID without I gives REDD.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of red, the most vividly coloured or ruddy of all.
